lastReply:
UPI has become India's default way to pay because it is free, fast and works almost everywhere. You scan a code or type a mobile number, enter your PIN, and the money moves between bank accounts in seconds, at any hour, on any day.

It also helped that it works on a basic smartphone, with no card machine or special hardware needed. A chai seller, a vegetable vendor and a big retailer can all take payments with the same printed QR code. Banks, wallets and apps like PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm all connect to the same system, so you are not locked into one app.

For many people it also feels safer than carrying cash. You get an instant record of every payment, and you never share card details with the shop. Sharing a bill with friends or paying a relative in another city takes a few taps.

Three main reasons:

Zero cost for most people: Everyday person-to-person and small shop payments carry no fee.
Speed and ease: One scan or one number, and the payment is done in seconds, around the clock.
Works everywhere: From street stalls to online shops, one system covers nearly every kind of payment.

Figures and rules change, so check the latest numbers before you quote them anywhere.
